title: Token Revision: Color Contrast, Typographic Scale, Spacing & Surface Depth for Dense Data UIs
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket consolidates a set of design-token updates focused on dense data surfaces (tables, charts, grid widgets) to improve legibility, reduce visual clutter, and unify perceived elevation across components. Changes cover: updated color palette ramps for neutral and semantic tokens, a refined typographic scale for small-data UIs, tighter spacing and radius tokens for compact components, and a simplified elevation/shadow system with fewer discrete layers and clearer contrast rules.

Goals:
- Improve text contrast at small sizes (12–14px) to meet WCAG AA for primary content and WCAG AAA for high-priority labels where feasible.
- Reduce perceived noise in dense tables and charts by tightening vertical rhythm and reducing shadow variance.
- Provide a compact token set that maps directly to component variants (compact / default / spacious).
- Make shadow/elevation behavior deterministic across platform (web, electron) to avoid platform-specific visual drift.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Color ramps: move neutral-600 -> neutral-700 for primary body copy at 14px when on light mode to increase contrast; keep neutral-500 for disabled and subdued copy. Trade-off: slightly darker UI overall but gains legibility in enterprise data views.
- Typographic scale: introduce two micro-scale steps (micro-1: 11px / 16px line-height, micro-2: 12px / 18px) for table cells and dense charts. This differs from the previous single small size to better map to real-world density needs. Trade-off: more tokens, but clearer usage guidance reduces misuse.
- Spacing & radius: collapse the previous eight-step radius scale into three functional tokens (sharp, rounded, pill) for components; reduce table row vertical padding by 12–18%. Trade-off: less granular control but easier to reason about density.
- Elevation/shadows: replace five subtle shadow variations with three semantic elevations (surface, raised, overlay) with explicit contrast deltas and CSS variables for cross-platform parity. Trade-off: some components will require visual retuning, but overall consistency improves.

Acceptance criteria:
- Token spec doc (Confluence) updated with new palettes, scale, spacing, radius, and elevation definitions and examples.
- Figma library updated and published: color tokens, type styles, spacing/radius tokens, and three elevation styles.
- Dev tokens exported via tokens.json and verified in the token build pipeline with snapshot tests.
- At least three representative components (primary button, table row, chart axis/legend) visually checked and approved in Figma and in a test environment (storybook).
- Accessibility audit: automated contrast checks pass for primary and secondary content; a remediation plan for any exceptions is documented.

Implementation plan / rollout:
1) Design: finalize token values and publish Figma draft (this ticket).
2) Tokens PR: generate tokens.json and open PR in repo redwood-design/tokens (link below).
3) Platform: land token-build changes and run visual snapshot tests across component library.
4) Canary: enable new tokens behind a feature flag for a small set of apps (console-data-grid, demo-dashboard).
5) Iterate: capture regressions (visual diffs, accessibility failures) and fix.
6) Full release: bump design-system package and ship in design-system-2026.03.

Migration notes for engineers:
- Provide a compatibility map: old_token_name -> new_token_name in the PR to make refactors straightforward.
- Add codemod script to replace deprecated spacing/radius tokens for common repos.
- Document recommended token subsets for dense vs. default layouts.

Open risks / unknowns:
- Some legacy consumer apps use hard-coded colors; migration may require additional app-level changes and coordination with product teams.
- Subtle chart rendering differences (canvas vs SVG) may make perceived contrast vary; we need to validate across renderers.
- Edge cases: dark mode tone mapping for high-contrast enterprise themes may require an extra token pass.

Next steps (short term):
- Address Marcus’ feedback on elevation opacity values by 2026-03-09. (done)
- Update tokens.json and open PR in tokens repo by 2026-03-11. (PR opened, link above)
- Schedule engineering sync to discuss codemods and rollout gating on 2026-03-15.

Notes on review feedback so far:
- Lina: asked for clearer examples of table header states (sorted / selected / focused) — added screenshots to Confluence.
- Priya: requested explicit CSS variable names for each elevation token to avoid platform mapping ambiguity — added to spec.
- Sabine: suggested slightly increased letter-spacing for micro-1 to avoid optical crowding at 11px; we agreed on +0.01em for micro-1.

Impacted components (quick list):

- "Tables (rows, headers, empty states)"
- "Charts (axis labels, legends, interaction highlights)"
- "Pills and badges"
- "Modal surfaces and dialogs (overlay elevation)"
